title: STEM Student Engagement with University Resources Builds Social Capital and Sense of Belonging: An Asset-Based Focus Group Study
text_snippet: STEM Student Engagement with University Resources Builds Social Capital and Sense of Belonging: An Asset-Based Focus Group Study Background. Attrition from STEM programs remains a persistent challenge for universities globally. To better support student success and socio-academic integration, universities have developed a range of curricular and co-curricular resources. Much emphasis has been placed on the benefits of these resources; however, less is known about how students recognize, access, and realize these benefits. Guided by a capital-mediated agency model, this asset-based focus group study examined how university-provided resources support undergraduate STEM students’ use of capital. We conducted four parallel focus groups with 21 students at a Norwegian university and analyzed narratives using thematic analysis. Results. Students described using both curricular and co-curricular resources to build personal/emotional, social, and human resource capital that helped them navigate academic and personal challenges. Curricular resources, including mandatory assignments, fieldwork, and laboratory activities, supported disciplinary training and opportunities to develop relationships with peers. title: The Impact of the Erasmus+ Programme on Participation in Democratic Life, Common Values and Civic Engagement: A Study on Portuguese and Slovenian Adult Education Organisations
text_snippet: The Impact of the Erasmus+ Programme on Participation in Democratic Life, Common Values and Civic Engagement: A Study on Portuguese and Slovenian Adult Education Organisations Active citizenship is one of the four main goals of adult education (AE) policy in the European Union (EU). While previous research has shown that EU AE policy has increasingly prioritised economic objectives, studies also suggest that Erasmus+ supports broader social goals. This study investigates how Erasmus+ in AE contributes to promoting active citizenship in Portugal and Slovenia. A mixed-methods design was employed, combining quantitative and qualitative data. Quantitative data were collected through a survey of 179 AE organisations, while qualitative data were obtained through document analysis, focus groups, and individual interviews with 17 representatives of AE organisations and 9 adult learners. The findings highlight the important role of Erasmus+ in supporting the social goals of European AE policy and suggest positive contributions to social inclusion, civic competences, critical thinking, and participation opportunities for adult learners, particularly among vulnerable groups. text_snippet: Longitudinal Associations Between Homework and Examination Performance in Engineering Mathematics Generative artificial intelligence has renewed questions about whether take-home homework remains associated with performance on supervised assessments. This retrospective longitudinal study analyzed 759 student records from 15 cohorts of an engineering mathematics course (2009–2025). Annual Pearson correlations between homework and quiz, midterm-examination, and final-examination scores were calculated with 95% confidence intervals and pooled within three periods using inverse-variance-weighted Fisher transformations. title: Preservice Early Childhood Teachers’ AI Literacy and Self-Efficacy in a Structured “Vibe Coding” Design Task: An Exploratory Pre–Post Study
text_snippet: Preservice Early Childhood Teachers’ AI Literacy and Self-Efficacy in a Structured “Vibe Coding” Design Task: An Exploratory Pre–Post Study This exploratory study examined a structured Vibe Coding task in preservice early childhood teacher education and its association with self-reported AI literacy, self-efficacy, attitudes toward AI, and technology acceptance. Vibe Coding was used in a qualified sense: participants created educational applications through natural-language prompting, then reviewed and revised the outputs. The task was implemented in two undergraduate courses using a convergent mixed-methods, single-group pre–post design without a comparison group. Quantitative analysis included 32 matched cases, while qualitative analysis drew on 26 reflective logbooks. All 32 participants also completed a researcher-designed, non-validated self-assessment rubric, reported descriptively. Paired-samples t-tests showed significant pre–post increases across all six self-report scales after Holm–Bonferroni correction. title: Reflective Practice in Arts-Based Learning: Teaching Adults with Intellectual Disabilities in Inclusive Higher Education
text_snippet: Reflective Practice in Arts-Based Learning: Teaching Adults with Intellectual Disabilities in Inclusive Higher Education This paper explores the development and delivery of an inclusive higher education programme for adults with intellectual disabilities within an Irish university. The programme was developed between two academic departments within an Irish University, to provide this student cohort with access to university life, enabling them to study and graduate alongside their peers. Central to the study is a module in arts-based communication, which aims to support students’ expressive, emotional, and social engagement in learning. Adopting a reflective, practice-based approach, the paper draws on the experiences of an educator involved in teaching on the programme. Through critical reflection on teaching practice, the study examines how arts-based pedagogies can enhance communication, participation, and inclusive learning environments for students with intellectual disabilities. The findings highlight the transformative potential of arts-based learning in supporting not only skill development but also confidence, self-expression, and relational engagement. title: Who Gets to Belong? Inclusive School Leadership and the Professional Experience of Early Career Teachers
text_snippet: Who Gets to Belong? Inclusive School Leadership and the Professional Experience of Early Career Teachers This study found that inclusive school leadership shaped early career teachers’ (ECTs’) professional belonging, but its influence depended on whether leaders’ relational intent was supported by the organisational conditions in which it was enacted. Inclusive leadership was understood as the relational and structural practices through which leaders foster voice, psychological safety, and equitable access to support. This study adopted an instrumental case study design, situated in an Australian primary school. Semi-structured interviews with five ECTs were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis, from which four themes were identified. Relational signalling from the principal shaped whether ECTs felt safe to voice uncertainty. Leadership functioned as emotional co-regulation in demanding moments, though its sustainability varied. Organisational routines produced a hidden curriculum through which ECTs learned when belonging was conditional. In high-stakes situations, guided participation actively drew ECTs into professional community practices. text_snippet: Rethinking Technology-Driven Sustainability Education Through Intermediality: Cultural Mediation, Literary and Artistic Humanities, and the Sustainable Development Goals The implementation of the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) across educational contexts has generated substantial research on pedagogies aligned with technology-driven sustainability education. Recent scholarship increasingly recognises that sustainability transitions require not only technological innovation but also cultural transformations capable of reshaping social norms, environmental imaginaries, and collective values. However, the processes through which sustainability meanings are mediated across different cultural and media environments remain insufficiently explored. title: Ubuntu Translanguaging as a Decolonizing Pedagogical Framework: Reimagining Multilingual Literacy Education for SDG 4
text_snippet: Ubuntu Translanguaging as a Decolonizing Pedagogical Framework: Reimagining Multilingual Literacy Education for SDG 4 This article advances Ubuntu translanguaging as a decolonizing pedagogical framework for multilingual literacy education, aligned with Sustainable Development Goal 4 (SDG 4). Drawing on Ubuntu philosophy and translanguaging theory, it conceptualizes Ubuntu translanguaging as a relational, asset-based framework that challenges linguistic hierarchies and affirms learners’ full linguistic resources. Grounded in Ghanaian educational contexts, the framework responds to deficit narratives that overlook the community-rooted pedagogies multilingual teachers already use, and shows how multilingual pedagogies strengthen comprehension, affirm identity, and expand equitable participation in education. Three questions guide the article: how Ubuntu translanguaging challenges colonial language hierarchies in curricula and policy, how it operationalizes SDG 4’s commitments to inclusion and equity, and how it can inform Global South–North research partnerships built on mutual growth. By centering indigenous epistemologies and positioning teachers as co-researchers and co-creators of knowledge, the framework offers a reciprocal model for achieving SDG 4.

title: Exploring Authentic Partnership in Distance Initial Teacher Education: Associate Teachers’ Perspectives from Aotearoa New Zealand
text_snippet: Exploring Authentic Partnership in Distance Initial Teacher Education: Associate Teachers’ Perspectives from Aotearoa New Zealand Partnership is widely treated as central to high-quality practicum in Initial Teacher Education, yet most research assumes local, ongoing relationships between Initial Teacher Education providers and schools. This study explores how Associate Teachers understand authentic partnership with a distance Initial Teacher Education provider in Aotearoa New Zealand, where placements are geographically dispersed, and partnerships are often short-term. Guided by an interpretivist qualitative design, the study drew on an online survey (n = 30), online focus groups (n = 7), and a live poll used as an elicitation tool (n = 7). Analysis identified four interrelated themes: communication as the foundation of partnership, clarity of roles and responsibilities, bridging theory and practice, and partnership and perceived support for Māori. title: When a Six Does Not Appear: Prospective Primary Teachers’ Questions for Informal Statistical Inference
text_snippet: When a Six Does Not Appear: Prospective Primary Teachers’ Questions for Informal Statistical Inference Teachers’ questions shape how students use data, representations, and uncertainty, yet little is known about the inferential opportunities embedded in questions formulated by prospective primary teachers using a provided representation. This study analyzed 133 questions produced by 45 prospective primary teachers for sixth-grade students in a semi-structured problem-posing task based on a dotplot of 60 die rolls in which no six appeared and two contrasting interpretations. title: Improving Students’ Digital Literacy in School Education: Insights and Practices from Physical Education Teachers
text_snippet: Improving Students’ Digital Literacy in School Education: Insights and Practices from Physical Education Teachers The integration of digital technologies into all areas of life, including school education, is a global megatrend. However, researchers note a lack of research on students’ digital literacy within school curricula, and specifically, it has not been examined in the context of school physical education. To address this research gap, this study explores physical education teachers’ practices, experiences, and perceived challenges in improving students’ digital literacy. In assessing students’ digital literacy, formative and summative approaches were identified. title: Literacies of Transnational Students of Color: A Critical Interpretive Synthesis Through an Intersectionally Informed Critical Race Theory Lens
text_snippet: Literacies of Transnational Students of Color: A Critical Interpretive Synthesis Through an Intersectionally Informed Critical Race Theory Lens Although racialization profoundly shapes global education, literacy scholarship concerning transnational students of Color (TSCs) frequently lacks an intersectional lens. This critical interpretive synthesis examines how existing studies conceptualize TSCs’ literacies and how their characterizations of race structurally and ideologically de/legitimize these practices. Following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, we systematically identified, screened, and selected empirical studies, then conducted a critical interpretive synthesis using an intersectionally informed Critical Race Theory framework, reported in accordance with ENTREQ. The review protocol was retrospectively documented and registered on the Open Science Framework. From 1282 initially identified records, 121 studies met the inclusion criteria. title: Navigating Inclusive Practices in Supporting Neurodivergent Learners in South African Under-Resourced Mainstream Schools: Perspectives from School Principals
text_snippet: Navigating Inclusive Practices in Supporting Neurodivergent Learners in South African Under-Resourced Mainstream Schools: Perspectives from School Principals Principals in mainstream schools occupy a pivotal yet underexplored position in supporting neurodivergent learners within resource-constrained settings. Guided by the transformational leadership theory lens, this study examines how mainstream school principals navigate neurodiversity support in resource-constrained school settings. A qualitative descriptive design, rooted in the interpretivist paradigm, was adopted. Data were collected from eighteen mainstream school principals from the Johannesburg Central district, using a quasi-structured questionnaire. Four themes emerged: identification of neurodivergent learners; support structures and inclusive practices; human, material resource and systemic constraints; and principals’ policy recommendations and visions for inclusive education in mainstream schools. The findings reveal a significant gap between policy intent and school-level practice. title: Cultivating a Regional Geoscience Learning Ecosystem: Systemic Equity and Cultural Change in California’s Central Valley
text_snippet: Cultivating a Regional Geoscience Learning Ecosystem: Systemic Equity and Cultural Change in California’s Central Valley The geosciences remain among the least racially diverse STEM fields, with limited progress over the past four decades. This article presents a case study of the San Joaquin Valley Geoscience Learning Ecosystem, a regional initiative designed to transform institutional culture and strengthen recruitment, engagement, and persistence for first-generation, low-income, and racially/ethnically diverse students in Geology and Environmental Science undergraduate majors at two Hispanic-Serving Institutions in California: Fresno State and the State Center Community College District. title: Variations in Equitable Sociocultural Interactions Across Learning Activities in Pre-K to Third-Grade Classrooms
text_snippet: Variations in Equitable Sociocultural Interactions Across Learning Activities in Pre-K to Third-Grade Classrooms This study used secondary data collected in public elementary schools from 2016 to 2019 to examine variations in equitable sociocultural interactions, measured by the Assessing Classroom Sociocultural Equity Scale (ACSES), among classroom formats (e.g., whole group, small group), content domains (e.g., language and literacy, math, science), and class sizes. The sample included 348 video recordings from 65 teachers. Results indicated that teachers made more connections to children’s home lives during language and literacy lessons compared to math lessons. Additionally, teachers provided children more Personalized Learning Opportunities during centers and small-group formats compared to whole-group formats. Analyses showed no variation in Inequitable Discipline or racially marginalized learners’ Participation and Engagement by content domain, classroom format, or class size. These findings point to the potential use of ACSES for measuring culturally responsive, equitable classroom management across multiple contents and classroom activity settings.

title: An Overview of Female Researchers: Demands, Job Resources, and Mental Health Among Brazilian University Faculty
text_snippet: An Overview of Female Researchers: Demands, Job Resources, and Mental Health Among Brazilian University Faculty Mental health problems among university faculty have been increasingly associated with intensified work demands, with women being particularly vulnerable due to persistent gender inequalities in academic careers. This study examined the perceptions of women faculty members at Brazilian public universities regarding work demands, organizational resources, and institutional practices aimed at promoting mental health and gender equity, using the Job Demands–Resources (JD-R) model as its theoretical framework. text_snippet: From Digital Integration to Digital Normalization: Generational Trends in Students’ Perception of Social Media Impact (2016–2022) This study examines how students perceive the influence of social media on everyday life across a seven-year period (2016–2022), focusing on two domains: aesthetic–consumer choices and lifestyle-related orientations. text_snippet: Automated Generation of Individualized Electrical Circuit Exercises Using Python and LTspice: Reducing Instructor Preparation Time This study presents a methodology for the automatic generation of individualized electrical circuit exercise booklets using Python and LTspice and examines the academic outcomes observed after its implementation and its estimated effect on instructor preparation time. title: Developing a Professional Learning Framework for Alternatively Certified Teachers: A Delphi Study of Knowledge, Skills, and Dispositions
text_snippet: Developing a Professional Learning Framework for Alternatively Certified Teachers: A Delphi Study of Knowledge, Skills, and Dispositions Teacher shortages and expanding alternative certification pathways have intensified the need for coherent support for teachers entering classrooms through nontraditional routes. This three-round Delphi study identified professional-learning priorities for newly alternatively certified teachers. Thirty-six K-12 teachers, administrators, and teacher educators in rural and semi-rural Montana completed all three rounds. Round 1 generated 120 open-ended responses, which were refined into 108 Round 2 statements; 97 statements advanced to Round 3. Item-level verification against the supplied Round 3 summary statistics showed that 53 of the 89 statements met both criteria: 7 knowledge, 19 skills, and 27 dispositions. title: How Should School-Based Educational Digital Games Be Evaluated? A Proposed Framework for Examining Experiences Beyond Isolated Metrics
text_snippet: How Should School-Based Educational Digital Games Be Evaluated? A Proposed Framework for Examining Experiences Beyond Isolated Metrics Educational digital games are increasingly incorporated into formal learning contexts. However, their evaluation often relies on isolated outcome measures that provide limited insight into how students experience, interpret, and assess gameplay. text_snippet: Differentiated Instruction and Learning Outcomes in Vocational Pharmacy Education: A Quasi-Experimental Study Differentiated instruction has been proposed as an effective approach for addressing learner diversity and enhancing learning outcomes. Cognitive performance, learning engagement, and cognitive load were assessed through quizzes, application exercises, questionnaires, and rating scales. title: Professional Development in Education: A Qualitative Study of Public School Teachers’ Perceptions of Meaningful Growth and Mandated Practice
text_snippet: Professional Development in Education: A Qualitative Study of Public School Teachers’ Perceptions of Meaningful Growth and Mandated Practice The present study investigates the professional development (PD) experience of ten public school teachers in British Columbia. The teachers are regular participants in school and district-based professional development (PD) programs. The research seeks to investigate whether PD is experienced as a genuine investment in professional growth or as time and resources that are wasted. Research suggests that traditional models often fail to produce deep, lasting change in practice. By investigating the professional and personal insights of teachers across grade levels and disciplines, the study identifies common themes in what makes PD meaningful, effective, or ineffective. These insights not only contribute to the understanding of teacher development but also offer practical implications for designing PD into the future that is relevant, engaging, and responsive to the realities of contemporary classrooms. The study contributes to ongoing discussions about how PD can more effectively support teacher learning as a socially mediated and contextually grounded process, affirming the value of aligning PD design with teachers’ professional agency and situated experience.

text_snippet: AI and Constructivist Pedagogy in TVET: A Scoping Review of Integration Mechanisms, Competencies, and Implementation Challenges The integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) into Technical and Vocational Education and Training (TVET) is reshaping instructional practices by enabling adaptive, learner-centered environments that support competency development. Reported in accordance with the PRISMA 2020 statement and PRISMA-ScR, this scoping review examines how AI-integrated constructivist pedagogy facilitates competency development in TVET contexts. Searches across six databases and a manual website search identified 11 studies published between 2016 and 2025, spanning multiple regions, TVET levels, and domains. Findings indicate that problem-based learning and project-based learning are the dominant constructivist approaches, supported by generative AI and intelligent tutoring systems. AI-enabled constructivist environments were associated with strengthened technical competencies and enhanced transferable competencies including critical thinking, collaboration, and career readiness. text_snippet: Understanding the Nature of Science (NOS): Insights from Pre-Service Teachers’ Engagement with Scientific Biographies The comprehension of the nature of science (NOS) is increasingly recognised as a crucial element of science education, and many countries have incorporated NOS-related elements into their national curricula. This development underscores the need to adequately prepare teachers to possess a thorough understanding of the fundamental principles of NOS. This article explores pre-service teachers’ understanding of NOS when engaging with scientific biography. Using biographies is proposed as a pedagogical strategy for embedding NOS within the curriculum. Grounded in the consensus view of NOS, this study evaluates students’ conceptualisations by analysing interviews and student presentations of the scientists’ life stories. The findings reveal variations in the students’ awareness concerning general aspects of NOS. text_snippet: Self-Perceived Ethical Knowledge in AI-Enhanced Teacher Education: Adaptation and Validation of a Scale for Chinese Preservice Preschool Teachers The increasing integration of artificial intelligence (AI) into early childhood education has led to ethical concerns regarding children’s privacy, fairness, and developmental appropriateness. While ethical knowledge is recognised as an important component of teachers’ professional knowledge, existing instruments such as the Technological Pedagogical Content Ethical Knowledge (TPCEK) framework were developed for preservice teachers in general and do not fully capture the ethical issues specific to AI-supported preschool education. In this study, we adapted and validated a Self-Perceived Ethical Knowledge Scale for Chinese preservice preschool teachers based on the eight ethics-related dimensions of TPCEK. A two-phase sequential design was employed. In Phase 1, a three-round modified Delphi study was conducted, involving 20 experts who refined an initial 40-item pool into a 33-item scale. In Phase 2, we examined the scale’s psychometric properties by performing an exploratory factor analysis (EFA) on a pilot sample (n = 289)—with factor retention corroborated by principal-axis parallel analysis—and confirmatory factor analysis (CFA) on a separate main-study sample (n = 583). text_snippet: A Study on Improving the Usability of an AI-Based Learning Tool to Support English Diary Writing for EFL Students AI-based writing support systems are increasingly being explored as tools for supporting English writing in educational contexts. title: AI Writing Assistants in Higher Education: A Comprehensive Review of Impact, Literacy, and Policy
text_snippet: AI Writing Assistants in Higher Education: A Comprehensive Review of Impact, Literacy, and Policy AI writing tools like ChatGPT, QuillBot, and Grammarly have reshaped university writing workflows. Controlled studies show gains in grammatical accuracy, student engagement, and self-efficacy, but none of the intervention studies retained in this review directly measured critical thinking or other higher-order outcomes, leaving concerns about overreliance largely untested rather than resolved. Synthesising 68 references published between 2008 and 2025, including 42 empirical studies, this narrative review examines how students utilise generative AI, its influence on core learning outcomes, and necessary institutional adaptations for policy and assessment. To address these shifts, the paper synthesises empirical findings across diverse study designs and proposes a seven-dimension AI literacy framework alongside practical design principles for effectively integrating AI tools into modern writing instruction.

title: Navigating Affective Cues in Video-Based Instruction: The Role of Instructor Emotions and Idiom Valence in English Idiom Acquisition
text_snippet: Navigating Affective Cues in Video-Based Instruction: The Role of Instructor Emotions and Idiom Valence in English Idiom Acquisition EFL vocabulary learning is an emotionally rich process, particularly in video-based instruction where learners encounter multiple affective cues. This mixed-methods study examined whether instructors’ emotional expressions and idiom valence influence EFL learners’ idiom acquisition and learning experience. A 3 × 3 within-subjects experimental design was adopted, manipulating instructor emotion (positive, neutral, and negative) and idiom valence (positive, neutral, and negative). Forty-five undergraduate EFL learners from a university in China participated in the study. After viewing each video, participants completed an immediate idiom recall test, a perceived learning experience scale, the self-assessment Manikin scale, a cognitive load scale and an open-ended questionnaire. The results showed that neither instructor emotion nor idiom valence had a significant main effect on immediate idiom recall. However, a significant interaction effect was observed, although follow-up comparisons did not identify a robust advantage for any specific congruent or incongruent condition. These findings provide implications for the emotional design of instructional videos in EFL vocabulary learning

title: Sources of Science Self-Efficacy in Primary and Secondary Students: A Systematic Review of Qualitative Research
text_snippet: Sources of Science Self-Efficacy in Primary and Secondary Students: A Systematic Review of Qualitative Research Efficacy beliefs shape how students think about science and engage with learning. A substantial body of research has linked science self-efficacy (SSE) to outcomes such as persistence, interest, and achievement, prompting interest in how these beliefs are formed and sustained via Bandura’s four sources: mastery experiences, vicarious experiences, social persuasion, and physiological and affective states. Only six mixed-methods studies have examined how SSE develops using qualitative data alongside quantitative approaches. This systematic review examines what these qualitative contributions add to our understanding of SSE and what they indicate about the value of further qualitative research. The analysis identifies how students’ beliefs about their scientific capabilities are shaped through classroom interactions, teacher practices, assessment systems, and school cultures. text_snippet: Cross-Cultural Adaptation and Preliminary Validation of a STEM Attitudes Scale for Spanish-Speaking Children This study presents the cross-cultural adaptation and preliminary validation of a STEM attitudes scale for Spanish-speaking primary-school students. A systematic review following PRISMA 2020 identified ten international instruments; a 27-item scale was selected for its comprehensive coverage of science, technology, engineering, and mathematics. title: Developing the Methodological Competence of Future IT Engineers in the Republic of Kazakhstan Through Problem-Oriented Learning
text_snippet: Developing the Methodological Competence of Future IT Engineers in the Republic of Kazakhstan Through Problem-Oriented Learning Kazakhstan’s transition toward Industry 4.0 and 5.0 increases demand for IT professionals capable of solving complex engineering problems. This study theoretically substantiated and empirically evaluated a didactic model for developing future IT engineers’ methodological competence through systemic problem-oriented learning. A quasi-experimental study involved 150 undergraduates from four Kazakhstani universities. In an integrated Smart Campus environment, students addressed authentic, industry-informed problems through an approach combining Challenge-Based Learning with the Four-Component Instructional Design model. Tasks included designing critical information infrastructure with provision for post-quantum cryptography and developing an intelligent energy-management system using fuzzy logic and the NSGA-III and MOEA/D algorithms. Performance on two engineering cases was independently evaluated using a 0–100 analytical rubric; scores were examined using the Shapiro–Wilk test, independent-samples Student’s t-tests, and Cohen’s d. The experimental group outperformed the control group in Case 1 (79.36 vs. 70.33; p = 0.003; d = 0.50) and Case 2 (80.61 vs. 71.12; p = 0.002; d = 0.53).

text_snippet: Tailoring Evidence-Based Mathematics Instruction: Developing Pre-Service Teachers’ Capacity to Support All Learners in Mathematics Persistent concerns about the mathematics achievement of culturally and linguistically diverse students with mathematics difficulties have intensified in recent years, underscoring the need for effective instructional strategies to support this growing student population. Research suggests that culturally and linguistically responsive (CLR) practices can address these disparities; however, many teachers enter the profession without the knowledge or skills to implement CLR practices effectively. text_snippet: An Integrative Assessment Framework for Virtual and Augmented Reality in Educational Settings The use of virtual and augmented reality (xR) in educational contexts opens up new pedagogical possibilities, but places high demands on planning, technology, and ethical responsibility. To date, no systematic tool is available to help educators and decision-makers evaluate use cases of immersive technologies in a structured manner. text_snippet: Digital–Relational Classroom Ecology: Teachers’ Perspectives on Digital Media, Self-Regulation, Reward Seeking, and Classroom Functioning Digital media have become deeply embedded in children’s everyday lives, but teachers encounter their effects, or perceived effects, through classroom behavior rather than through screen-time measures alone. title: Research-Based Practices for Early Childhood Instruction on the Nature of Scientific Knowledge
text_snippet: Research-Based Practices for Early Childhood Instruction on the Nature of Scientific Knowledge It has long been recommended that the nature of scientific knowledge (NOS) be incorporated into science lessons, but unfortunately, this is not yet the case. Many researchers recommend that NOS be embedded in science lessons as early as possible, as research has shown that, given appropriate instruction, young children can conceptualize ideas about NOS, which can serve as a building block toward scientific literacy. In this manuscript, we describe the importance of teaching NOS to young children and share research indicating which strategies have been successful in improving young children’s conceptions of it. Our research question is, “What are the best practices for teaching NOS in early childhood settings?”. We then share results from a systematic literature review using the PRISMA approach of current research in NOS (within the past fifteen years) and describe successful interventions, such as the importance of explicit reflection and the incorporation of ideas through literacy connections, scientific inquiry, and STEM integration. text_snippet: REWIND: Environmental Role-Playing and Student Engagement in Climate Change Education Climate change education increasingly calls for experiential and participatory approaches capable of engaging students cognitively, emotionally, and behaviorally. text_snippet: Digital Dependency and Academic Identity Among Postgraduate Students in the Era of Generative AI Generative artificial intelligence has become embedded in everyday university life, often faster than institutional guidance has developed. title: Mapping Consensus in Evidence-Informed Initial Teacher Education Core Curricula
text_snippet: Mapping Consensus in Evidence-Informed Initial Teacher Education Core Curricula A robust, evidence-informed knowledge base for initial teacher education (ITE) is essential for preparing prospective teachers. Although a growing body of research addresses the content of ITE curricula, there is little consensus on what constitutes the minimal agreed knowledge for ‘learning how to teach’. This study reports a comparative analysis of two published, evidence-informed core ITE curricula. Items appearing in both were compiled into the Minimal Agreed Knowledge Set (MAKS) and corroborated against two research literature: teacher-effectiveness research and cognitive/educational psychology. The MAKS comprises 52 knowledge elements, organised under eight instructional principles and one category of general statements on teaching and learning, and represents areas of convergence between two frameworks from a shared, evidence-informed policy tradition. It is intended as a tool for ITE providers to review and refine their own curricula, rather than as a prescriptive programme. Implications for curriculum development and directions for future research on MAKS are discussed.

title: Development and Validation of the Instrumental Musical Self-Concept Scale for High School Students
text_snippet: Development and Validation of the Instrumental Musical Self-Concept Scale for High School Students In the field of musical learning, self-concept has received increasing attention in recent years. However, previous research in Spain has largely focused on students enrolled in specialized professional and higher music education, while instrumental musical self-concept in compulsory secondary education remains underexplored. To address this gap, the present study developed an ad hoc scale specifically designed to assess instrumental musical self-concept among secondary school students. The final sample consisted of 980 students from 14 educational centers in Aragón and Navarra (Spain). The results provide evidence supporting the internal structure and internal consistency of the 16-item Instrumental Musical Self-Concept Scale for High School Students, organized into four theoretically interpretable factors. These findings contribute to the study of instrumental musical self-concept in Spanish secondary education and provide an instrument whose psychometric properties can be further examined in independent samples and through additional sources of validity evidence.

title: Attractiveness by Design and by Communication: A Desk-Based Analysis of Croatian Teacher Education Programmes
text_snippet: Attractiveness by Design and by Communication: A Desk-Based Analysis of Croatian Teacher Education Programmes Teacher education increasingly competes for candidates, which makes programme attractiveness a question of alignment between what programmes signal publicly and what their curricula offer. This study examines that alignment in the 14 Croatian university programmes through which candidates holding a disciplinary qualification acquire pedagogical competences (the consecutive model). Using a comparative desk-based design, qualitative content analysis and structured comparison were applied to publicly available sources through two lenses: communicated attractiveness (how programmes publicly frame the teaching profession, the student experience, and the transparency of demands and support) and designed attractiveness (what the curricula and intended learning outcomes formally offer). Alignment between the two dimensions was classified into four patterns. title: Pedagogical Interventions That Support Self-Regulated Learning in Secondary School Students: A Systematic Literature Review
text_snippet: Pedagogical Interventions That Support Self-Regulated Learning in Secondary School Students: A Systematic Literature Review Self-regulation of learning (SRL) is a key skill for secondary school students, placing them as active and conscious agents of their own learning. It enables learners to plan, monitor, and evaluate their progress, fostering autonomy and responsibility. Teachers play a crucial role by designing pedagogical interventions that guide and support students across different learning stages toward achieving personal goals. However, further research is needed to understand how different pedagogical strategies have been used to support SRL in secondary school contexts. This study conducted a systematic literature review using PRISMA with two goals: (1) to identify and describe teaching strategies in pedagogical interventions for SRL in secondary education, and (2) to analyze how these interventions support students’ self-regulation. From 12 selected papers, seven pedagogical approaches were identified. The findings highlight the diversity of pedagogical strategies, technologies and assessment practices and indicate the need for clearer methodological guidance, teacher preparation and future comparative research on SRL interventions.

title: Social Media Use and Academic Procrastination Among University Students: A Systematic Review of Empirical Studies
text_snippet: Social Media Use and Academic Procrastination Among University Students: A Systematic Review of Empirical Studies The widespread use of social media among university students has raised increasing concerns regarding its possible association with academic behaviors, including procrastination. This systematic review aimed to synthesize empirical evidence on the relationship between social media use and academic procrastination among university students. Following the PRISMA 2020 guidelines, a systematic search was conducted in Web of Science, Scopus, PsycINFO, ERIC, and PubMed and was last updated in August 2026. Quantitative peer-reviewed empirical studies examining the association between social media use and academic procrastination in university populations were included. Twenty-nine articles comprising 30 study samples met the inclusion criteria. Overall, the evidence indicated a recurrent positive association between social media use and academic procrastination, although the magnitude and form of the relationship varied across distinct operationalizations, including general use, problematic use, addiction, social media disorder, and platform- or behavior-specific forms of use. title: Navigating Disruption: A Transformative Learning Theory Examination of Faculty Perceptions of Generative Artificial Intelligence in Academic Practices
text_snippet: Navigating Disruption: A Transformative Learning Theory Examination of Faculty Perceptions of Generative Artificial Intelligence in Academic Practices Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) tools such as ChatGPT have rapidly entered higher education, challenging longstanding norms around authorship, assessment, and disciplinary expertise. While early GenAI scholarship has largely emphasized student outcomes, adoption trends, and academic integrity, comparatively little empirical work has examined how faculty and staff make sense of this disruption over time. title: Does Shared Reading Promote Cognitive Development? A Literature Review
text_snippet: Does Shared Reading Promote Cognitive Development? A Literature Review Shared reading is recognized as an educational method that promotes language development and emergent literacy during early childhood. text_snippet: Conceptualizing School Leaders as Organizers of Systems and Resources This study examined distributed leadership at a school that underwent transformation over a ten-year period beginning in 2014. Building on theory, we focused on capacity building as a key construct in distributed leadership, connecting it to the vision for school transformation and to the distribution of responsibilities outside central administration. title: Higher Education Institution Choice: A Systematic Review of Contemporary Trends and Decision Factors
text_snippet: Higher Education Institution Choice: A Systematic Review of Contemporary Trends and Decision Factors Higher education institution (HEI) choice is increasingly influenced by digitalisation, internationalisation, intensified institutional competition, widening participation, and financial uncertainty. title: Digital Skill Alignment over Time: The Dynamic Digital Skill Realisation Framework for Graduate Employability
text_snippet: Digital Skill Alignment over Time: The Dynamic Digital Skill Realisation Framework for Graduate Employability Higher education is expected to develop digital capabilities that support graduate employability, but the labour-market relevance of those capabilities can change between acquisition and employment entry. This conceptual article develops the Dynamic Digital Skill Realisation Framework (DDSRF) to explain that transition as a time-sensitive process rather than a fixed skills match. A theory-building synthesis was constructed through targeted purposive searches spanning higher education, digital skills, graduate employability, labour-market alignment, skill decay and obsolescence, signalling, employer judgement, and unequal employment outcomes. The contribution lies not in introducing new individual constructs, but in integrating them into a temporally explicit process. The framework distinguishes capability formation from initial alignment, capability-side skill decay from demand-side obsolescence, and skill signalling from employer recognition and valuation. title: Social–Emotional Competence Across Arab Educational Subsystems in Israel: A Comparative Analysis of Sector, Gender and SES
text_snippet: Social–Emotional Competence Across Arab Educational Subsystems in Israel: A Comparative Analysis of Sector, Gender and SES Social–emotional competence (SEC) is an important factor contributing to students’ academic success and psychological well-being. While research on SEC is widespread, studies within the unique demographic and ethnic context of the Arab minority in Israel remain scarce. This study examined SEC levels across three distinct educational subsystems (General Arab, Druze, and Bedouin), alongside gender and socioeconomic status (SES). title: Teacher Wastage in Pakistan: How Education Systems Employ Teachers but Lose Instructional Capacity
text_snippet: Teacher Wastage in Pakistan: How Education Systems Employ Teachers but Lose Instructional Capacity Pakistan has expanded teacher recruitment across its public education system over the past decade, yet policy and monitoring reports continue to document substantial rural, school-level, and subject-specific teacher shortages. In this article, I extend the concept of educational wastage to teachers, shifting attention from the loss of teachers to the loss or underuse of instructional capacity among formally employed teachers. I identify three forms of teacher wastage. Pre-deployment wastage occurs when appointment does not result in classroom instruction because teachers cannot take up or sustain placements, political influence directs placements away from school staffing needs, or teachers recorded as employed do not teach. Structural wastage occurs when teachers in schools are diverted from or misaligned with instruction through transfer instability, non-academic duties, or subject or grade-level misassignment. text_snippet: Exploring University Students’ Experiences of Using Conversational Artificial Intelligence for Emotional and Relational Support in Experiences of Loneliness University students’ loneliness has remained a persistent concern in the years following the COVID-19 pandemic and correlates with multiple mental health issues, yet little is known about how university students experiencing loneliness use conversational artificial intelligence (CAI) for emotional and relational support. title: Teacher Mental Health and Well-Being from the Pandemic to the Post-Pandemic Era: A Systematic Review of Interventions, Policies, and Persistent Gaps

This systematic review synthesizes 66 peer-reviewed studies and policy reports (2020–2026). Meta-analyses of 54 studies (256,896 teachers, 22 countries) found stress prevalence at 62.6%, anxiety at 36.3%, and depression at 59.9%. text_snippet: When Nature-Based Activities Become Participatory: Pedagogical Mediation of Young Children’s Participation Child participation is central to rights-based early childhood education, yet it is often interpreted as verbal expression, choice-making or general engagement. Nature-based activities may broaden young children’s participation because they offer sensory, material and spatial forms of expression. title: Curriculum Internationalization in Higher Education: Evolution, Fragmentation, and Emerging Critical Perspectives from a Systematic and Bibliometric Review
text_snippet: Curriculum Internationalization in Higher Education: Evolution, Fragmentation, and Emerging Critical Perspectives from a Systematic and Bibliometric Review Curriculum internationalization has become a relevant field in higher education because it connects pedagogical design, intercultural learning, global competencies, and critical debates on knowledge production. title: Mathematics Education and Sustainability (2010–2025): A Mixed Bibliometric Mapping and Critical Curricular Analysis
text_snippet: Mathematics Education and Sustainability (2010–2025): A Mixed Bibliometric Mapping and Critical Curricular Analysis This study examines research trends at the intersection of school mathematics education and education for sustainability during the period 2010–2025. Using a mixed bibliometric design based on 970 documents indexed in Scopus published in English, Spanish, and Portuguese, the study combined quantitative bibliometric mapping with complementary qualitative content analysis. The results reveal sustained growth in publications, organized primarily around STEM/STEAM approaches and technology-oriented educational frameworks. Keyword and collaboration networks show thematic diversification alongside a concentration of scientific production in Global North countries. Qualitative analysis suggests that sustainability is frequently incorporated as an applied or contextual dimension rather than as an integrated curricular component of school mathematics, although some emerging studies demonstrate deeper forms of socio-environmental integration. The findings highlight the need for research with greater geographical diversity, higher empirical rigor, and a deeper pedagogical approach.

text_snippet: Teacher Support for Curriculum Adaptation and Inclusive Assessment in Rural South African Secondary Schools Inclusive education depends on teachers’ capacity to adapt curriculum and assessment to accommodate diverse learner needs. text_snippet: Technology-Mediated Scaffolding to Support Critical Thinking in Pre-Service Teachers’ Academic Writing Developing critical thinking skills (CTS) is a central goal of higher education, yet pre-service teachers often receive little explicit guidance on how to apply them in academic or professional writing. text_snippet: Implementation Characteristics, Students’ Perceptions, and Instructional Impact of Haptic-Enabled Learning Experiences in Higher Education: A Systematic Literature Review By enabling active hands-on exploration of structures and phenomena that are invisible or impractical to manipulate in real life, haptic technologies have the potential to enhance learning across multiple fields of higher education. However, a comprehensive understanding of their implementation, instructional impact, and students’ perceptions remains limited. This systematic review synthesizes evidence from 101 studies published between 2000 and April 2026 across 11 educational fields, extending previous reviews beyond their predominant focus on health sciences. Only 24 studies explicitly grounded haptic-enabled instruction in theory, most commonly embodied cognition. title: The Compliance Trap and Relational Anchors in Structured Instructional Leadership
text_snippet: The Compliance Trap and Relational Anchors in Structured Instructional Leadership Instructional leadership is often displaced by compliance requirements, operational demands, and formal evaluation. This qualitative secondary analysis examined how teachers and principals described organizational pressures and relational practices during a 14-day Build Rapport, Inspire Feedback, Celebrate Success, and Exceed Results (BICE) leadership cycle across five Southern California public charter schools. Data included open-ended survey responses from 33 experienced teachers, interviews with nine teachers, and interviews with six principals. A role-by-source matrix and constant comparison were used to examine demands that displaced developmental work, valued leadership practices, and convergence or tension across participant groups. Two cross-cutting themes emerged. The compliance trap described how urgent operational and accountability demands displaced coaching, recognition, and relationship-building. text_snippet: Process-Oriented Assessment of Project-Based Learning in Analytical Chemistry: Tracking Students’ Experimental Decision-Making Pathways Learning analytical chemistry requires not only mastery of analytical and calculation methods but also the ability to make consistent experimental decisions. This study tested a process-oriented assessment framework based on the experimental decision-making pathway (EDMP) construct and the analysis of student-specific decision-making trajectories. A quasi-experimental study involved 60 second-year students, 30 each in a project-based learning group and a control group with a traditional laboratory format. title: Dissonance in Interactions with Parents: A Qualitative Study on Vulnerability and Trust and Implications for the Professional Development of Early Childhood Educators
text_snippet: Dissonance in Interactions with Parents: A Qualitative Study on Vulnerability and Trust and Implications for the Professional Development of Early Childhood Educators The expectation of establishing an educational partnership with parents poses challenges for both parents and early childhood educators (ECEs). Structural conditions and diverging orientations often complicate cooperation between educators and parents. This exploratory qualitative interview study with 15 ECEs examines which situations in their interaction with parents they find challenging. Based on qualitative content analysis, tense situations in interactions with parents are interpreted through the lenses of vulnerability and dissonance theory. The results show that ECEs experience different dissonances, vulnerabilities, and varying forms of trust in their work with parents. While experienced ECEs report role-related tensions (dissonances), younger ECEs describe relational strains with parents. The findings highlight profession-specific challenges that are discussed in terms of their implications for ECEs’ (further) professional development.

title: Rural LGBTQ+ College Students in U.S. Higher Education: An Asset-Based Examination of Engaging Interactions and Institutional Environments
text_snippet: Rural LGBTQ+ College Students in U.S. Higher Education: An Asset-Based Examination of Engaging Interactions and Institutional Environments Rural LGBTQ+ college students remain understudied in higher education. This study provides one of the few large-scale, multi-institutional quantitative examinations of this student population. Using 2023–2025 National Survey of Student Engagement (NSSE) data from nearly 300,000 first-year and senior students across 872 four-year institutions in the U.S., we combined variable-centered regression analyses and person-centered cluster analyses to examine engaging interactions with others and engaging institutional environments. We found distinct patterns of engagement associated with rural background, LGBTQ+ identity, and their intersection. Rural students reported less frequent engagement in some interactions with others but generally had more positive perceptions of their environment. LGBTQ+ students, however, had more frequent engaging interactions with others but a less favorable view of their environment. text_snippet: An Exploration of the Self-Efficacy of Secondary School Pre- and In-Service Teachers to Teach Sustainable Food Literacy Education is critical to achieving the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Sustainable food literacy provides a powerful context for transformative Education for Sustainable Development, enabling real-world learning in secondary schools. This exploratory cross-sectional study used the Norwegian Teacher Self-Efficacy Scale to examine the perceived self-efficacy of home economics pre- and in-service teachers (N = 173) to teach sustainable food literacy, administered via a global digital survey. Through content analysis and parametric and non-parametric descriptive and inferential statistical analyses, the study reveals that teachers’ familiarity with the SDGs intersects with their willingness to integrate them into teaching. Self-efficacy for teaching sustainable food literacy was generally moderate to high, with lower levels among pre-service teachers. text_snippet: Comparing Quality in Academia Utilizing Data Envelopment Analysis: The Relationship Between Quantitative and Qualitative Indicators at Institutions of Higher Education Israel’s system of higher education, like many national research evaluation systems worldwide, contends with a constant tension between quantitative metrics and the need to promote significant scientific excellence. This article explores the relationship between quantitative and qualitative indicators at academic institutions by utilizing the data envelopment analysis (DEA) technique. text_snippet: Curriculum Design and Evaluation of Data Science Track for Management Students The growing demand for data science competencies across professional fields creates a need for curricula that enable management students to develop analytical skills while navigating increasingly complex technological environments. This study examines the design and evaluation of a three-year Data Science track embedded within an undergraduate management program. title: When Confidence Masks Conceptual Gaps: Examining Teachers’ Knowledge of Graphs and Procedural Approaches to Teaching
text_snippet: When Confidence Masks Conceptual Gaps: Examining Teachers’ Knowledge of Graphs and Procedural Approaches to Teaching Graphs are a conceptually demanding yet foundational component of school mathematics, yet their teaching is often shaped by procedural routines that can obscure weak conceptual understanding. text_snippet: From Individual Chatbot Interaction to the Virtual Tutor with Physical Presence: Comparing Educational Interaction Models with Conversational AI Conversational artificial intelligence can provide individual study support, but the educational significance of its responses depends on how they are examined and used. title: Resources Shaping Science Teachers’ Design and Implementation of Scientific Argumentation Instruction: A Systematic Review
text_snippet: Resources Shaping Science Teachers’ Design and Implementation of Scientific Argumentation Instruction: A Systematic Review Scientific argumentation is a core scientific practice recognized by multiple national science standards, yet many science teachers experience challenges integrating it into their classrooms.
